paragraphs: Humanity distinctively embodies both expressions of creation, fusing the invisible and the visible into a single living being. The soul—invisible—fulfills itself in such things as intelligence, beauty, goodness, order, and harmony; the body—visible—draws on food and energy to exist and act within the world. In humanity, the two expressions of creation are bound together: spirit dwells within flesh, will finds expression through action, and life itself becomes the place where the creator’s presence is extended into creation.

This synthesis is affirmed across traditions. Genesis presents humanity as formed from the dust of the ground and animated by the breath of God, becoming a “living soul”— body and spirit fused in a single act of creation [20]. Plato’s Timaeus describes the soul as formless and immortal, sharing the same divine substance as the universe’s own soul, and only afterward placed into a body of physical matter—merely a temporary vessel [21]. From the East, the Da Dai Liji holds that humanity is born of the union of Heaven and Earth’s vital energy [24]. Together, these voices affirm one truth: humanity is where spirit and flesh, invisible and visible, converge into a single living presence.
